bc_gate.text: The road to Birmingham is closed. Bridge inspection. We are inspecting it very thoroughly.
Spirit Stone, they say. Hester in York has it. Something about a crypt. Come back when you've seen a bit more of the country.

bc_boater.text: She's called the Mildred. I'm called Dave. I've been up and down these canals for thirty years and I still can't get the lock gate to stop squeaking.
The Dudley Tunnel is nearly two miles long and the old boatmen walked the boats through on their backs, legging it along the roof. Imagine your hamstrings.

bc_museum.text: Over at the Living Museum in Dudley they've moved real Black Country buildings brick by brick. A chip shop, a chapel, a pub. The chip shop does a very good faggot and peas.
Our dialect has a thousand years behind it. Black Country speech has kept some old English forms the rest of England dropped. Some say 'thee' and 'thou' still.

bc_pigeon.text: Racing pigeons. A good bird will fly five hundred miles home in a day. They know the way back to the loft better than I do to the pub.
Half the lofts in the Black Country are on allotments. The other half are in someone's back garden, behind a fence and a dog.

bc_ironmaster.text: Iron's in our blood. Coal under the ground, ironstone, limestone, all within a few miles of each other. That's why the Black Country happened here, and not in Cornwall.
My grandad made chain at Cradley Heath. My gran made it too. She was better at it.
